best.mechanism: Normalize dictionary words once. For each normal-monomial product C A D E, repeated modes between C and D or between A and E force contractions in A∩D; an unavailable forced contraction makes the product zero. Enumerate only optional contractions. For a contracted subset S, compute the sign using the uncontracted inversion count plus independent per-mode corrections and |S|(|S|-1)/2. Construct surviving canonical groups directly, accumulate their Gram coordinates, and add transposes for off-diagonal coordinates. Homogeneous charge makes every product charge zero, so canonical transposition has positive adjoint sign.
best.assumptions: Words obey the stated degree and homogeneous-charge contract. Flags use 0 for annihilation and 1 for creation. Modes are hashable and consistently sortable. All coefficients use exact Python integer arithmetic. No oracle, external state, task-specific answers, or prepopulated cache is required.
best.failure_cases: Performance improvement is unverified. Products with few forced contractions may incur enough sign-calculation and allocation overhead to outweigh pruning. Construction still visits every upper-triangular dictionary pair, and output storage can dominate. Mixed-charge dictionaries violate the positive-transpose-sign assumption and are outside the input contract.

best.hypothesis: Constructing symmetric coefficients by canonical adjoint orbits can reduce cold construction time by eliminating the second product normalization for every off-diagonal coordinate. This is an unmeasured algorithmic proposal.
best.mechanism: Homogeneous charge makes every product charge zero. A canonical charge-zero monomial has equally many creators and annihilators; its adjoint swaps their mode lists with positive sign because the two reversal signs cancel. For each i<j, normalize only B_i^dagger B_j, then assign each adjoint orbit the sum of its two coefficients. Self-adjoint monomials receive twice their coefficient. Diagonal products are emitted directly. Zero sums are never inserted, and kernel results are never mutated.
best.assumptions: The supplied car_kernel callable implements its stated exact CAR contract. All dictionary words have the same particle-number charge and degree at most three. Modes support the ordering and hashing required by that kernel. No assumption is made about dictionary ordering, support structure, duplicates, or canonical input ordering.
best.failure_cases: Mixed-charge dictionaries invalidate the sign-free adjoint rule and are outside the contract. Partner caching and orbit bookkeeping may outweigh avoided normalization for small dictionaries or inexpensive kernel hits. Partner-cache memory grows with encountered canonical monomials. No execution, independent verification, or timing measurement was performed.
